title: Ordinalia
subtitle: The Cornish mystery cycle: Origo Mundi, Passio Domini Nostri Jhesu Christi, Resurrexio Domini Nostri Jhesu Christi
author: Anonymous (Cornish)
note: Middle Cornish text of the three plays from Edwin Norris, The Ancient Cornish Drama (Oxford: University Press, 1859, 2 vols; Origo Mundi and Passio in vol. 1, Resurrexio in vol. 2), transcribed from the Internet Archive scans of the University of Toronto copies and checked against a second scan. Norris's preface, English version (held separately as ordinalia-norris), notes, Cornish grammar, vocabulary and appendices, his footnotes, the margin line numbers, the manuscript folio marks and the running heads are left out. The speakers' names and the Latin stage directions are kept as printed, each on a line of its own; in the Passio the mid-line dot is kept. Norris's spelling is kept (v for u, w for the vowel in some words).
blurb: The three Middle Cornish mystery plays of the late fourteenth century, the longest body of medieval Cornish: the Creation to Solomon, the Passion of Christ, and the Resurrection, in about 8,700 lines of rhymed stanzas.
